To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the changes in the membrane potential of mast cells are dependent on the ionic composition of the medium.
the changes in membrane potentials induced in mast cells by different stimuli are dependent on the ion composition of the medium.

(i) the plasma membrane of rat peritoneum mast cells depolarizes in the presence of the ionophore gramicidin, and this depolarization is not affected by the presence of the Na+, K+ pump inhibitors ouabain, vanadate and amiloride; (ii) the plasma membrane potential of the mast cells hyperpolarizes in the absence of external sodium; and (iii) the plasma membrane depolarizes when the external osmolarity increases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of different stimuli on the membrane potential and the role played by the ionic composition of the medium in the changes in membrane voltage.
the study of the effects of different stimuli on the plasma membrane potential of rat mast cells.
the effects of various stimuli on the membrane potential in rat mast cells in different ionic media.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the membrane potential of the mast cell is determined by the Na+/K+-ATPase activity and the Na+/Ca2+-exchanger, the latter being dependent on intracellular calcium.
the membrane potential changes induced by the different stimuli in the mast cells studied are the result of a complex interplay of different mechanisms.
the changes of membrane potential of mast cells are a function of the ionic composition of the extracellular medium and the nature of the stimulus.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the membrane of rat peritonea mast cells is a highly selective and active membrane, which is able to respond in a very specific way to several stimuli.
the changes in the membrane potential induced with the different stimuli are related to the changes in the ionic composition of the medium.
